source.title: Inferences on a multidimensional social hierarchy use a grid-like code

confidence_rationale: Direct human fMRI evidence that entorhinal/hippocampal-mPFC circuitry represents a genuinely MULTI-DIMENSIONAL abstract relational space (two independent axes of a social hierarchy) and computes novel direct trajectories across it for never-directly-compared entities -- the closest empirical analog available to a topology holding more than one relation/dimension at once. Confidence held at 0.72 rather than higher because the two dimensions are both instances of the same relation TYPE (ranked ordering), not qualitatively different relation types (requires vs. enables vs. conflicts-with), and the task is discrete two-alternative choice, not action selection during ongoing goal pursuit.
failure_signatures: The reconstructed cognitive map is built from directly-observed pairwise comparisons in each of two dimensions and then used to infer novel pairwise relations by geometric interpolation within the SAME two-dimensional space -- it does not demonstrate an agent adding a qualitatively new relation type (e.g. 'conflicts with') to an existing topology, which is the specific claim-shaped idea under evaluation.

The task is a static, discrete inference/decision task (which of two people ranks higher) rather than an active goal-pursuit task in which the relational structure must be discovered or revised online -- so it speaks to the representational format of a multidimensional relational map, not to the discovery-through-action mechanism in Section 8 of the intake.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Human participants learned a two-dimensional abstract social hierarchy from discrete pairwise comparisons. When later asked to infer never-directly-compared relations, entorhinal cortex and medial prefrontal cortex showed a grid-like (hexagonally periodic) code over the reconstructed 2D space, and this grid-like signal was linked to decision-value computations in mPFC and temporoparietal junction during the inference.
mapping.ree_translation: Evidences that the same grid-cell-like machinery SD-004 leans on for spatial/action-object mapping generalizes to representing and computing over MULTIPLE simultaneous abstract relational dimensions, not a single relation. This is direct support for the idea that the hippocampal-entorhinal backbone could in principle hold several independent relation axes over the same set of represented entities/possibilities at once (a structural precondition for the candidate general topology, which needs several DISTINCT relation types co-present, not just several dimensions of one relation type).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Gathered to evaluate the NOT-YET-REGISTERED general-relational-possibility-topology candidate claim. This paper shows the entorhinal/hippocampal system can hold and interpolate over a genuinely multidimensional abstract space, which weakens the objection that hippocampal machinery is limited to a single linear/path relation -- but 'multidimensional' here still means several axes of the SAME kind of relation (rank/similarity), not the qualitatively different relation types (requires, enables, prevents, substitutes-for...) the candidate claim proposes. It is evidence that the substrate has more representational headroom than a single path graph, not evidence that REE's specific typed-relation extension is what fills that headroom.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI, healthy adult participants, discrete two-alternative forced-choice inference task over a learned abstract (non-spatial, non-physical) social hierarchy; task-to-REE transfer risk is moderate (human abstract cognition maps reasonably to REE's aim of general-purpose relational representation, but the task itself is far simpler than continuous embodied goal pursuit).

confidence_components.notes: source_quality high (Nature Neuroscience, pre-registered-style discrete design, converging fMRI signatures in two regions). mapping_fidelity moderate-high for the 'general relational substrate, not spatial-only' half of SD-004, moderate-low for the specific typed-multi-relation topology extension. transfer_risk moderate: human abstract social cognition to an artificial agent's action-possibility topology is a real but not extreme domain jump.
